text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Lower house of parliament makes it easier to deport foreigners who commit crimes in Germany.
- German Council of Economic Advisers, known as "the five wise men", predicts growth of 2.5 percent for 1997.
- Court issues arrest warrants against former members of East German politburo, including ex-leader Egon Krenz.
- Construction Minister Klaus Toepfer plans reform of state-supported housing projects.
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem says contributions to public penision schemes will rise next year.
HANDELSBLATT
- Five wise men say Germany will miss deficit target laid down in Maastricht Treaty for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
- Deutsche Telekom share offer five times oversubscribed, banking sources say.
- Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer indicates room for manoeuvre in Maastricht criteria.
- German Trade Union Federation (DGB) moves to create new statement of basic principles.
- Deutsche Lufthansa may be completely privatised this year, government budget plans show.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Pension contributions to rise above 20 percent for first time, Bluem says.
- Government plans deficit of less than 56 billion marks in 1997, Sueddeutsche Zeitung has learned.
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and Greens criticise government plans for cuts in research spending.
DIE WELT
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU/CSU) plan to make fight against Mafia key theme in 1998, year of next general elections.
- President Roman Herzog says his forthcoming trip to China will concentrate on political and cultural ties.
- Germany has lost appeal as an industrial location since 1980, German Confederation of Industry (BDI) says.
